discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies with WMAP, establishing the standard cosmological model

nominees.name: David N. Spergel
nominees.affiliation: Simons Foundation and Princeton University, USA

motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe, conceived and led by Charles Bennett with Lyman Page responsible for key instrumentation and David Spergel for the cosmological interpretation, turned cosmology into a precision science. Its full-sky maps of temperature and polarization anisotropies, with exquisite control of foregrounds and systematics, determined the geometry, age, baryon and dark-matter densities of the universe to percent precision, measured the epoch of reionization, and detected the departure from scale invariance of the primordial fluctuations predicted by inflation. Combined with supernova distances, WMAP independently confirmed dark energy and fixed the six-parameter Lambda-CDM model that underpins all of modern cosmology. This was a new observational capability, followed through by a small leading team with exceptional statistical care, and it changed how we measure the cosmos. The 2006 prize recognized COBE's discovery of anisotropy; WMAP delivered its physical meaning.
